setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Open tasks
steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8): the Masks page opens for CH01. Turn E1 one detent. From any page, E1 opens Channel tasks, with the page you came from highlighted, here Masks. The nine tasks, top to bottom, are 1 Masks, 2 Trig params, 3 Output, 4 Clock, 5 Merge modes, 6 Merge Shape, 7 Harmony, 8 Device and 9 History.

steps.title: Scroll down to Harmony
steps.caption: With the list open, E1 and E2 both scroll it, one row per detent. Turn E1 two detents to row 3, Output, then turn E2 four detents: Clock, Merge modes, Merge Shape, and Harmony, row 7, is highlighted.

steps.title: Scroll back up to Masks
steps.caption: Turn E2 four detents back up the list to Output (row 3), then turn E1 four detents the same way. The highlight stops on Masks, row 1, and the list does not wrap.

steps.title: Open Trig params
steps.caption: Turn E2 one detent down to Trig params (row 2) and press K3. The Trig params screen opens for CH01.

steps.title: Return to the list with E1
steps.caption: Turn E1 one detent. Channel tasks reopens with Trig params highlighted, the page you came from, so E1 always brings you back to the task list at your current page.

steps.title: Open Trig params again
steps.caption: Press K3 to open Trig params again. The header reads TRIG PARAMS CH01.

steps.title: Scroll to History (row 9)
steps.caption: Turn E1 to reopen Channel tasks, then turn E2 down to row 9. History, the last row, is highlighted and its value reads OPEN >.

steps.title: Open History
steps.caption: Press K3. The History screen opens. Every task in the list opens its own screen this way.

steps.title: Open Clock (row 4)
steps.caption: Turn E1 to open Channel tasks from History, scroll up to row 4, Clock, and press K3. The Clock screen opens for channel 1.

steps.title: Scroll to Device (row 8)
steps.caption: Turn E1 to open Channel tasks again, then turn E2 to row 8. Device is highlighted and its value reads OPEN >.

steps.title: Open Device
steps.caption: Press K3. The Device screen opens for channel 1, where its output is chosen.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: A new empty project that has just started: stopped, Record off, channel 1 selected and no step held. The Channel editor is showing: its header reads NOTE MASKS CH01. The first step visits the page keys before you hold a step.

steps.title: Visit the page keys
steps.caption: Tap each page key in turn and watch the header follow. Scale (4,8) opens the Scale Editor, SCALE SLOT 01. Pattern (5,8) cycles Trig, Note, then Velocity: three taps reach PATTERN VELOCITY PAT01 CH01. Song (6,8) opens SONG PLAYBACK SONG 01. Channel (3,8) brings you back to NOTE MASKS CH01.

steps.title: Select channel 3
steps.caption: Tap channel 3 at (3,1). The header now reads NOTE MASKS CH03.

steps.title: Hold a step
steps.caption: Press and hold step 5 at (5,4). The header reads CH03 ST05: ST05 means step 5 of the selected channel. While the step is held, edits on this Masks page apply to step 5 only.

steps.title: Edit while the step is held
steps.caption: With step 5 still held, turn E2 to the Note cell and turn E3 one detent up. The Note cell changes from X to C-2 and the header still reads CH03 ST05, so the edit belongs to step 5 only.

steps.title: Release the step
steps.caption: Let go of step 5. The header drops back to NOTE MASKS CH03 and edits apply to the whole channel again.

steps.title: The channel value is unchanged
steps.caption: Look at the Note cell now. It still reads X, the channel's own value, so the C-2 you set lives on step 5 alone.

steps.title: Open the Clock page
steps.caption: Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, scroll to Clock and press K3. The Clock page for CH03 is showing.

steps.title: Hold a step from the Clock page
steps.caption: Press and hold step 9 at (9,4). While it is held the screen switches to that step's Masks, header NOTE MASKS CH03 ST09, whichever page you were on.

steps.title: Return to the parent screen
steps.caption: Release step 9. The screen returns to the Clock page, the page you were on before you held the step.

scenes.title: Protect playback from a stray tap

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase through the test MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 with C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The channel range is steps 1-4, the tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 and the sequencer is stopped. Every Mosaic option is at its default, so Shift press to stop is Off. The Device page for CH01 is showing.

steps.title: Start playback
steps.caption: Press Play/Stop (1,8). The phrase starts and the MIDI stream carries the four notes.

steps.title: A tap stops by default
steps.caption: With Shift press to stop Off, press Play/Stop (1,8) again after under a second. The sequencer stops, the MIDI stream goes silent and every sounding note is released.

steps.title: Turn Shift press to stop on
steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Shift press to stop and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.

steps.title: Start with the option on
steps.caption: Close the menu and press Play/Stop to start. Starting is never blocked: the phrase plays.

steps.title: Ignore a short stop tap
steps.caption: Tap Play/Stop again after under a second. The tap is ignored and the phrase keeps playing.

steps.title: Hold briefly without stopping
steps.caption: Press and hold Play/Stop for 0.9 seconds, then release. This is still shorter than the one-second threshold, so playback continues.

steps.title: Stop with Shift
steps.caption: Hold K1 and tap Play/Stop. With Shift held, a short tap stops playback and releases its notes.

steps.title: K3 is not a shift key
steps.caption: Tap Play/Stop to start again. Hold K3 and tap Play/Stop: K3 is not a shift key, so playback continues.

steps.title: Stop with a long press
steps.caption: Hold Play/Stop alone for 1.1 seconds. Playback stops, because a hold of one second or more counts as a long press.

steps.title: Turn Shift press to stop off
steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Shift press to stop and turn E3 left to Off. The row reads Off.

steps.title: Ordinary tap stop is back
steps.caption: Close the menu, start playback and tap Play/Stop: a short tap stops it again.

scenes.title: Keep a named project and recover it

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody through a MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI notes 60, 62, 64 and 65. The sequencer is stopped and the Device page for CH01 is showing. The project has never been saved under a name, so no new or newB file exists.

steps.title: Hear the original melody
steps.caption: Press Play (1,8), listen, and press it again to stop. The melody is C, D, E, F: MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65.

steps.title: Find Save project
steps.caption: Tap K1 to open the norns menu, choose PARAMS, then MOSAIC, and scroll to Save project.

steps.title: Save the default name
steps.caption: Press K3 to open the name entry. It starts on the suggested name, new, with OK selected, so press K3 again to accept it. Mosaic writes the project file and its parameter file under that name. Tap K1 to close the menu.

steps.title: Open Save project again
steps.caption: Tap K1 and scroll to MOSAIC > Save project once more.

steps.title: Save another name
steps.caption: Press K3 to open the name entry. Turn E3 left to the letter row, turn E2 one detent to B and press K3 to add it, so the name reads newB. Turn E3 right to the bottom row, turn E2 right to OK and press K3. A second, separate save is created, and both saves, new and newB, now hold the melody C, D, E, F. Tap K1 to close the menu.

steps.title: Edit the melody
steps.caption: Press Pattern (5,8) twice: the first press shows the trig page and the second the note page. Press (4,3) to raise step 4 from F to G. Tap Channel (3,8) to return to the Channel editor and press Play (1,8): the melody is now C, D, E, G, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 67.

steps.title: Let autosave preserve both names
steps.caption: Leave Mosaic stopped and untouched for about a minute until the idle autosave runs. A third file, autosave, is written. The saves new and newB are not touched.

steps.title: Cancel a save
steps.caption: Tap K1 and scroll to MOSAIC > Save project. Press K3 to open the name entry, then press K2 to cancel. No project file changes. Tap K1 to close the menu.

steps.title: Overwrite only the chosen name
steps.caption: Open Save project again, press K3, then K3 again to accept the name new and confirm replacing it. The save new now holds the edited melody C, D, E, G. The save newB is unchanged and still holds C, D, E, F.

steps.title: Find Load project
steps.caption: Tap K1, then scroll to MOSAIC > Load project.

steps.title: Load the preserved phrase
steps.caption: Press K3 to open the file picker, choose newB.ptn and press K3. The original melody returns. Close the menu and press Play to hear MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65.

steps.title: Load the overwritten phrase
steps.caption: Load new.ptn the same way. The edited melody plays MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 67. The save newB is still in the file list.

scenes.title: Restrict every note to five degrees

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major through the test MIDI device. The channel range is steps 1-4, the tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 (sixteenth-note steps, one sixth of a second each) and the sequencer is stopped. Every Mosaic option is at its default, so Lock all to pentatonic is Off. Lock all to pentatonic forces every note you play onto a five-note subset of the chosen scale, so each scale step below changes which five notes survive.

steps.title: Extend the pattern to seven steps
steps.caption: Open the Pattern editor (5,8), which starts on the trig page. Tap steps 5, 6 and 7 on the trig row, (5,4), (6,4) and (7,4). Press (5,8) again for the note page and press the rising diagonal (1,7), (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2), (7,1): one note per step, scale degrees I-VII, C D E F G A B. The note page now shows a rising diagonal.

steps.title: Set the velocities of steps 5 to 7
steps.caption: Press (5,8) for the velocity page and tap (5,1), (6,2) and (7,3): the velocity bars for steps 5, 6 and 7 light up.

steps.title: Set the range to seven steps
steps.caption: Return to the Channel editor (3,8), hold step 1 (1,4) and tap step 7 (7,4). Steps 1 to 7 light up and step 8 stays dark, so the channel range is steps 1-7.

steps.title: Hear the plain major scale
steps.caption: Press Play and listen to two loops with Lock all to pentatonic at its default Off: all seven plain C major degrees sound, 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71.

steps.title: Turn Lock all to pentatonic on
steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, scroll to Lock all to pentatonic and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.

steps.title: Switch off the other two locks
steps.caption: Scroll down to Lock random to pent. and turn E3 left to Off, then do the same for Lock merged to pent. Both rows read Off, so Lock all to pentatonic is the only option that can change a pitch.

steps.title: Snap major to pentatonic
steps.caption: Press K2 to step back, then K1 to close the menu, and play the seven steps again: 60, 62, 64, 64, 67, 69, 72. Major keeps degrees 1/2/3/5/6 (C D E G A). F falls to E and B rises to C because only those five are allowed.

steps.title: Pick Harmonic Major
steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent and press K3. The Scale row reads Harmonic Major.

steps.title: Step to Harmonic Major
steps.caption: Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Harmonic Major keeps the same degrees as Major, 1/2/3/5/6, but its sixth is A-flat: 60, 62, 64, 64, 67, 68, 72. F falls to E, A-flat stays and B rises to C.

steps.title: Minor uses its own five notes
steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Minor and press K3. Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. The minor family keeps degrees 1/3/4/5/7 (C E-flat F G B-flat): 60, 63, 63, 65, 67, 67, 70. D snaps up to E-flat and A-flat snaps down to G.

steps.title: Pick Harmonic Minor, then Melodic Minor
steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Harmonic Minor and press K3, return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play. Then open the Scale Editor again, turn E3 one more detent and press K3: the Scale row reads Melodic Minor.

steps.title: Hear Harmonic and Melodic Minor
steps.caption: Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Harmonic Minor and Melodic Minor give the same pitches: 60, 63, 63, 65, 67, 67, 71. Only the top note differs from Minor, B-flat becoming B. In Harmonic Minor A-flat snaps down to G; in Melodic Minor A sits exactly between G and B, and an equal-distance note snaps to the lower pitch, so it also lands on G.

steps.title: Step to Dorian
steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Dorian and press K3. Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Dorian keeps degrees 1/2/4/5/7 (C D F G B-flat): 60, 62, 62, 65, 67, 70, 70. E-flat falls to D and A rises to B-flat.

steps.title: Step to Phrygian
steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Phrygian and press K3. Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Phrygian keeps degrees 1/3/4/6/7 (C E-flat F A-flat B-flat): 60, 60, 63, 65, 68, 68, 70. D-flat falls to C and G rises to A-flat.

steps.title: See the lower boundary snap
steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Lydian and press K3. Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Lydian keeps degrees 2/3/5/6/7 (D E G A B), so the tonic C snaps down to the B below it: 59, 62, 64, 67, 67, 69, 71.

steps.title: Step to Mixolydian
steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Mixolydian and press K3. Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Mixolydian keeps degrees 1/2/4/5/6 (C D F G A): 60, 62, 65, 65, 67, 69, 69. E rises to F and B-flat falls to A.

steps.title: Step to Locrian
steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Locrian and press K3. Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Locrian keeps degrees 2/3/4/6/7 (D-flat E-flat F A-flat B-flat), so the tonic C snaps up to D-flat and G-flat snaps down to F: 61, 61, 63, 65, 65, 68, 70.

steps.title: Turn Lock all to pentatonic off
steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, scroll to Lock all to pentatonic and turn E3 left to Off. The row reads Off.

steps.title: All seven Locrian pitches return
steps.caption: Close the menu and play. All seven plain Locrian pitches return: 60, 61, 63, 65, 66, 68, 70. Musical tip: leave Lock all to pentatonic On when a pattern is random or generative, so every note lands in a five-note set that stays consonant in any scale, and Off when you want the full seven-note colour.

scenes.title: Start from the chosen scale degree

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped and a MIDI keyboard is connected as Mosaic's input. Every Mosaic option is at its default, so Map scale to white keys and the three Honour switches are Off, and the Scale Editor is on C major.

steps.title: Turn on Map scale to white keys
steps.caption: Play some keys on the keyboard: each sounds the note you pressed, because nothing is mapped yet. Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control. Select Map scale to white keys and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.

steps.title: Play the white keys in C major
steps.caption: Close the menu and play the white keys from C3 up to C4 on the keyboard. In C major they sound as written: 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71, 72. The MIDI strip lists the notes Mosaic sent.

steps.title: Choose natural minor in the Scale Editor
steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 two detents and press K3. The Scale row reads Minor, natural minor.

steps.title: Play the white keys in natural minor
steps.caption: Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play the white keys again: they now follow C natural minor, 60, 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72 (C D E-flat F G A-flat B-flat C).

steps.title: Set degree II
steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (4,8) again, turn E2 one click to Degree, turn E3 one detent and press K3. Degree reads ii°. Degree picks which scale note the keyboard's C starts on.

steps.title: Set rotation 2
steps.caption: Turn E2 to the Rotation row, turn E3 two detents and press K3. Rotation reads r2. Rotation moves the top keys down an octave.

steps.title: Set global transpose +2
steps.caption: Tap the global transpose fader on the grid at its lowest value, then tap its increment button fourteen times, and return to the Channel editor (3,8). The Scale overview lists Transpose +2, which shifts everything.

steps.title: Nothing applies yet
steps.caption: The three Honour switches are still Off, so none of this is applied yet: the white keys still play 60, 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72.

steps.title: Turn on Honour scale degree
steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control. Select Honour scale degree and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.

steps.title: Start from the chosen scale degree
steps.caption: Close the menu and play C3 to C4 again. Key C now plays the scale's second note: 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72, 74 (D E-flat F G A-flat B-flat C D). Rotation and transpose stay unapplied, so you can start a phrase from degree II without changing the scale.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped and a MIDI keyboard is connected as Mosaic's input. Map scale to white keys is On and the scale is C natural minor. The Scale Editor holds degree II, rotation 2 and global transpose +2, and Honour scale degree is On, so the white keys C3 to C4 play 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72, 74. Honour scale rotations and Honour scale transpose are Off.

steps.title: Turn on Honour scale rotations
steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control. Select Honour scale rotations and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.

steps.title: Rotate the keyboard voicing
steps.caption: Close the menu and play C3 to C4 again. Rotation 2 turns the top of the scale upside down: the last two white keys before the octave, the A and B keys, sound an octave lower, 58 and 60 instead of 70 and 72, giving 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 58, 60, 74. The first five keys do not change. Use it to play a bass note or an inverted voicing of the same scale shape from the keys you already know.

scenes.title: Apply the scale transpose to live input

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped and a MIDI keyboard is connected as Mosaic's input. This lesson continues from the degree and rotation lessons. Map scale to white keys is On and the scale is C natural minor, with degree II, rotation 2 and global transpose +2 set in the Scale Editor. Honour scale degree and Honour scale rotations are On and Honour scale transpose is Off, so the white keys C3 to C4 play 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 58, 60, 74.

steps.title: Turn on Honour scale transpose
steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control. Select Honour scale transpose and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.

steps.title: Apply the scale transpose to live input
steps.caption: Close the menu and play C3 to C4 again. The scale's global transpose of +2 now applies to everything you play, so every key sounds two semitones higher than in the start: 64, 65, 67, 69, 70, 60, 62, 76. The MIDI strip lists the notes Mosaic sent.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The sequencer is stopped. A MIDI controller on input port 1, channel 1 is connected and sends relative CC 20: a value of 63 means one step down and 65 one step up. Nothing is mapped yet and the velocity mask is Off (X).

steps.title: Find the velocity mask parameter
steps.caption: Tap K1, choose PARAMS, open Mosaic Midi Mapping and turn E2 to the selected-channel velocity parameter. The selected row reads Selected Ch. Velocity.

steps.title: Switch to MAP mode
steps.caption: Hold K1 and press K3 to switch from EDIT to MAP mode. The list now names each parameter by its id, sel_ch_vel for this one, and nothing is mapped yet.

steps.title: Open the map editor
steps.caption: Press K3 to open the map editor. Learn is selected, and the editor lists cc 100, ch 1, dev 1 EMIDI, in 0 to 127, out -1.0 to 1.0, accum no and echo no.

steps.title: Arm Learn
steps.caption: Press K3 on Learn. The row reads LEARNING while the editor waits for the controller.

steps.title: Move the controller
steps.caption: Move the controller so it sends CC 20. The editor learns it and the cc row reads 20, with input port 1 and channel 1.

steps.title: Set Input low to 1
steps.caption: Turn E2 five clicks to the first number of the in row, Input low, and turn E3 one click right. It reads 1.

steps.title: Set Input high to 2
steps.caption: Turn E2 one click to the second number of the in row, Input high, and turn E3 left until it reads 2. Inputs 1 and 2 are the two steps a relative controller sends.

steps.title: Turn Accum on
steps.caption: Turn E2 three clicks to accum, past the out row, and turn E3 one click right. Accum reads yes and out still reads -1.0 to 1.0, so each message adds to the value instead of setting it.

steps.title: Assign the map
steps.caption: Press K2 to assign. Back in the list, sel_ch_vel now shows 20:1:1, the controller's CC 20 on channel 1 of input port 1.

steps.title: Return to EDIT mode and leave PARAMS
steps.caption: Hold K1 and press K3 to return to EDIT mode, press K2 twice to leave the group, then tap K1 to return to Mosaic. The controller is now mapped to the velocity mask.

steps.title: Open the Masks page
steps.caption: Turn E1 to Channel tasks, choose Masks with E2 and press K3, then turn E2 to the Vel cell. It reads X, Off, because nothing has moved it yet.

steps.title: Turn the controller up
steps.caption: Send CC 20 with value 63 once, which leaves Off where it is, then value 65 five times: each message steps the velocity mask up one. The Vel cell rises from X to 4.

steps.title: Hear velocity 4
steps.caption: Press Play and stop. The MIDI strip shows all four notes at velocity 4.

steps.title: Turn the controller down
steps.caption: Send CC 20 with value 63 once more. The Vel cell drops to 3.

steps.title: Hear velocity 3
steps.caption: Press Play and stop. The MIDI strip shows all four notes at velocity 3.

scenes.title: Carry a slide across the loop boundary

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped. Every Mosaic option is at its default, so Wrap param slides is Off, and nothing is locked yet.

steps.title: Assign CC 1 to a trig slot
steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Trig params and assign the device's CC 1 to a trig slot. The channel default for CC 1 is 63.

steps.title: Lock step 1 to 24
steps.caption: Press K3 to confirm the CC 1 assignment and K2 to go back. Hold step 1 and turn E3 to 24. Slot 1 shows 24 with an L in its corner while the step is held. Release the step.

steps.title: Lock step 3 to 96
steps.caption: Hold step 3 and turn E3 to 96. Slot 1 shows 96 with the L. Release the step.

steps.title: Lock step 4 to 48
steps.caption: Hold step 4 and turn E3 to 48. Slot 1 shows 48 with the L. Step 2 gets no lock and keeps the channel default, 63.

steps.title: Turn a step slide on
steps.caption: Hold step 1 and press K3. Slot 1 shows 24 with an S in its corner, so the lock on step 1 now slides toward the next lock. Release the step.

steps.title: Turn the step slide off again
steps.caption: Hold step 1 and press K3 again. The S goes and the L returns, so step 1 jumps again. Release the step.

steps.title: Play without a slide
steps.caption: Play two loops. With no slide, CC 1 does not glide from 24 to 96. Each loop the MIDI strip shows only 24 on step 1, 63 on step 2 (the channel default, because step 2 has no lock), 96 on step 3 and 48 on step 4.

steps.title: Slide the last lock
steps.caption: Hold step 4 and press K3 to give the last lock (48) a slide. Slot 1 shows 48 with the S.

steps.title: Give the last lock no destination
steps.caption: Wrap param slides is still Off, so there is no later lock to slide toward: CC 1 stays at 48 through step 4, and the first lock, 24, is recalled when the loop restarts. Play and listen for the value changing abruptly at the loop point.

steps.title: Turn Wrap param slides on
steps.caption: Tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Wrap param slides and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.

steps.title: Slide to the first lock
steps.caption: Tap K1 to return to Mosaic and play. The step-4 slide now runs from 48 down to 24 across one sixteenth-note step (one sixth of a second): CC 1 passes 40 and 32 and reaches 24 exactly with the first note of the next loop. Look for those CC values in the MIDI strip. Use this for a cyclic sweep, such as a filter that falls back to its start with no jump at the loop point.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped and the Device page for CH01 is showing. Channel 2 is not set up yet: you will make it a steady timing reference. Trigless locks is at its default On.

steps.title: Check Trigless locks, then set up the channels
steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC. Trigless locks reads On, its default, so locks on steps without a trig will still be sent. Press K2, then K1 to leave the menu. Set up channel 2 as the timing reference: tap (2,1), open Channel tasks > Device, point it at the second MIDI port, give it pattern 1 at (1,2) and range steps 1-4 (hold (1,4), tap (4,4)). It will play C D E F on MIDI channel 2 on every loop whatever you do to channel 1. Then tap channel 1 (1,1), open Channel tasks > Trig params and assign CC 1 to the first slot.

steps.title: Lock step 1 to 24
steps.caption: Press K3 to confirm CC 1 and K2 to go back. Hold step 1 and turn E3 to 24. Slot 1 shows 24 with an L in its corner while the step is held. Release the step.

steps.title: Lock steps 2 to 4 to 48, 72 and 96
steps.caption: Do the same on the other steps. Hold step 2 and turn E3 to 48, hold step 3 for 72 and hold step 4 for 96. Slot 1 reads 96 with the L while step 4 is held, so every step now carries its own CC 1 value.

steps.title: Add Trig probability
steps.caption: Assign Trig probability to the second slot, so you can silence channel 1's notes and see only its CC 1 stream beside channel 2's steady notes.

steps.title: Probability 0 silences the notes, not the locks
steps.caption: Set Trig probability to 0 so channel 1's notes never sound, and play two loops. All four steps have trigs, so CC 1 goes out at every step (24, 48, 72, 96) even though no note plays: look for those four CC values each loop in the MIDI strip, beside channel 2's steady notes.

steps.title: Remove the third trig
steps.caption: Open the Pattern editor (5,8), tap step 3 to remove its trig, and return to the Channel editor (3,8). Play. With Trigless locks On, a lock on a step with no trig is still sent: the MIDI strip shows CC 1 still sending 72 at step 3, so automation keeps moving through rests, for example a filter sweep under a sparse rhythm.

steps.title: Keep a lock ahead of its accepted note
steps.caption: Hold step 4 and turn E3 to set its Trig probability lock to 100, then play. Step 4's note (F3, 65) now sounds, with its CC 1 lock (96) sent just before it. Steps 1 and 2 stay silent, and step 3 still sends its 72. The scene Skip automation on rests plays the same steps with Trigless locks Off, for comparison.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped and the Device page for CH01 is showing. Channel 2 is not set up yet: you will make it a steady timing reference. Trigless locks is at its default On.

steps.title: Turn Trigless locks off
steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Trigless locks and turn E3 left to Off. The row reads Off.

steps.title: Assign CC 1
steps.caption: Press K2, then K1 to leave the menu. Set up channel 2 as the timing reference: tap (2,1), open Channel tasks > Device, point it at the second MIDI port, give it pattern 1 at (1,2) and range steps 1-4 (hold (1,4), tap (4,4)). It will play C D E F on MIDI channel 2 on every loop whatever you do to channel 1. Then tap channel 1 (1,1), open Channel tasks > Trig params and assign CC 1 to the first slot.

steps.title: Lock step 1 to 24
steps.caption: Press K3 to confirm CC 1 and K2 to go back. Hold step 1 and turn E3 to 24. Slot 1 shows 24 with an L in its corner while the step is held. Release the step.

steps.title: Lock steps 2 to 4 to 48, 72 and 96
steps.caption: Do the same on the other steps. Hold step 2 and turn E3 to 48, hold step 3 for 72 and hold step 4 for 96. Slot 1 reads 96 with the L while step 4 is held, so every step now carries its own CC 1 value.

steps.title: Add Trig probability
steps.caption: Assign Trig probability to the second slot, so you can silence channel 1's notes and see only its CC 1 stream beside channel 2's steady notes.

steps.title: Probability 0 silences the notes, not the locks
steps.caption: Set Trig probability to 0 so channel 1's notes never sound, and play two loops. All four steps still have trigs, so CC 1 still goes out at every step (24, 48, 72, 96) even with Trigless locks Off: look for those four CC values each loop in the MIDI strip, beside channel 2's steady notes. A probability of 0 is not a rest: only a removed trig is.

steps.title: Remove the third trig
steps.caption: Open the Pattern editor (5,8), tap step 3 to remove its trig, and return to the Channel editor (3,8). Play. With Trigless locks Off, a lock on a step with no trig is skipped: the MIDI strip shows CC 1 sending 24, 48 and 96 but not 72, the value on step 3.

steps.title: Keep a lock ahead of its accepted note
steps.caption: Hold step 4 and turn E3 to set its Trig probability lock to 100, then play. Step 4's note (F3, 65) now sounds, with its CC 1 lock (96) sent just before it. Steps 1 and 2 stay silent, and step 3 still sends no value. The scene Keep automation on rests plays the same steps with Trigless locks On, for comparison.

scenes.title: Decide whether a slow channel restarts

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped. Song mode is On, and the song has one slot with a 64-step global length. Every other option is at its default: Reset on song seq change is On and Reset on pattern repeat is Off.

steps.title: Make a slow channel
steps.caption: Hold step 1 and tap step 3 to set the range to steps 1-3. On Channel tasks > Clock set Clock Mod to /9. One step now lasts nine sixteenths (1.5 seconds), so the three notes 60, 62, 64 cycle every 4.5 seconds, while the song pattern repeats every 64 steps (10.7 seconds). The two never line up, which is what makes the reset visible.

steps.title: Both resets off: the phase carries on
steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC. Make sure Song mode is On, then turn Reset on song seq change Off and Reset on pattern repeat Off. Close the menu, press Play and let it run for 24 seconds, then stop. The phrase carries on across each repeat: 60 62 64 60 62 64 60 62, then 64 at 12 seconds. Read the note times in the MIDI strip.

steps.title: Reset on song seq change alone
steps.caption: Turn Reset on song seq change On and play 24 seconds. A pattern that is only repeating is not restarted by a song change, so the phrase still carries on, with the same note times as before.

steps.title: Reset at each repeat
steps.caption: Turn Reset on song seq change Off and Reset on pattern repeat On, close the menu and play 24 seconds. At each 64-step boundary, 10.7 and 21.3 seconds, the slow channel restarts: note 60 sounds exactly at the boundary instead of waiting for the old cycle. Compare the note times in the MIDI strip with the first run.

steps.title: Turn both reset options on
steps.caption: Turn Reset on song seq change On as well, so both options are On, and play 24 seconds. The channel restarts at each repeat, as in the last step.

steps.title: Song mode off: no reset
steps.caption: Select Song mode and turn E3 left to Off; both reset options stay On. Close the menu and play 24 seconds. With Song mode Off the slot is not stepped by the song, so neither reset applies: the phrase runs continuously again, with 64 at 12 seconds.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped. Channel 1 has been made slow: its range is steps 1-3 and Clock Mod is /9, so one step lasts 1.5 seconds and the phrase 60, 62, 64 cycles every 4.5 seconds. Song mode is On and the song has two 64-step slots, 10.7 seconds each. Slot 2 is a copy of slot 1 with the channel octave raised by one, so it sounds an octave higher: C4 D4 E4 are 72, 74, 76. Slot 1 is selected, so on the Song editor (grid (6,8)) its LED (1,1) is bright and (2,1) dim. Both reset options are Off.

steps.title: Watch the slot change
steps.caption: Press Play. After 10.7 seconds, at the 64-step slot change, the slot LEDs swap brightness: (2,1) is now the bright one.

steps.title: Both resets off: the phase carries across two slots
steps.caption: Let it play to 23 seconds, then stop. The phrase keeps its place across the slot change: slot 2 starts on E4 (76) at 12 seconds, not C4. Read the note times in the MIDI strip.

steps.title: Restart at a changed song slot
steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Reset on song seq change and turn E3 right to On; Reset on pattern repeat stays Off. Close the menu and play 23 seconds. At each slot change, 10.7 and 21.3 seconds, the channel restarts on its first step: C4 (72) sounds exactly at the change, an octave above slot 1's C3, and the slot LEDs swap as before.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major. The sequencer is stopped, Rate is /1 and every Mosaic option is at its default. The norns clock is internal at 90 BPM. A separate MIDI device is connected on port 1 and will send clock at 100 BPM when Mosaic follows it. The PARAMS menu is closed.

steps.title: Begin with internal clock
steps.caption: Tap K1 to open the norns PARAMS menu and open the CLOCK group. Source reads internal: Mosaic keeps its own tempo of 90 BPM.

steps.title: Select MIDI clock
steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent. Source reads midi. Mosaic now follows incoming MIDI clock, Start and Stop from the connected device and waits for them, so its own tempo no longer sets the speed.

steps.title: The other device sends clock
steps.caption: You do nothing in this step: the connected device sends clock, a Start, more clock, then a Stop. Mosaic stays silent through the first clock pulses, begins when Start arrives, plays the phrase at the sender's 100 BPM and halts when Stop arrives. The MIDI strip below lists the notes, 0.15 seconds apart, one sixteenth at 100 BPM.

steps.title: Return to internal
steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent back down to put Source on internal. Mosaic is on its own clock again.

steps.title: Bring the tempo back to 90 BPM
steps.caption: Turn E2 to the tempo row. It reads 100 BPM: while Source was midi the incoming clock set the tempo, and switching Source back does not restore your own. Turn E3 ten detents down to bring it back to 90 BPM, the tempo the project used before.

steps.title: Play on the internal clock
steps.caption: Close the menu and press Play. The notes are again one sixth of a second apart, the pace of 90 BPM, as the MIDI strip shows.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Starting point
steps.caption: Channel 1 has pattern 1 assigned over steps 1 to 4, but pattern 1's trigs have been cleared, so no step is lit. A MIDI keyboard is connected on port 1 and Record is off. The norns clock source is internal; an external MIDI clock at 100 BPM is available. Mosaic records each note onto the step that is playing when the note arrives, so recording needs a running clock: this lesson borrows the external one. If you have no external clock, start Mosaic's own clock with Play (1,8) and arm Record the same way.

steps.title: Follow the external clock
steps.caption: Tap K1 to open the norns PARAMS menu, open the CLOCK group and turn E3 so Source reads midi. Mosaic now follows the external 100 BPM clock.

steps.title: Record two notes
steps.caption: Close the menu and tap Record (2,8) to arm recording. While the external clock runs, play MIDI note 72 at velocity 90 and then note 79 at velocity 80 on the keyboard. Each note lands on the step playing when it arrives. Tap Record again to disarm. The grid shows steps 2 and 4 lit, and steps 1 and 3 empty. Which steps light depends on when you press, so your own take may land elsewhere.

steps.title: Back to the internal clock at 90 BPM
steps.caption: Tap K1, open the CLOCK group and turn E3 back so Source reads internal. Following the external clock left the tempo at 100 BPM, so turn E2 to the tempo row and turn E3 until it reads 90 BPM; any tempo works, the notes' spacing simply follows it.

steps.title: Replay and hear the rhythm
steps.caption: Close the menu and tap Play (1,8). The channel plays note 72 at velocity 90, then note 79 at velocity 80, repeating, as the MIDI strip lists. The two notes sit on steps 2 and 4, so they alternate every two steps: at 90 BPM with the default Rate /1 that is one third of a second apart.

setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.title: Arm parameter recording
steps.caption: With CC 1 assigned and its channel value at 63, tap Record (2,8). Its grid cell blinks while recording is armed. The Trig Params screen still shows the channel value 63. Start playback and turn E3 to 64; Mosaic records that value on the next eligible steps.

assertion.characterisation: The captured armed blink phase is grid level 12; the renderer test marks its blink output as -4.
The captured armed blink phase is grid level 12; the renderer test marks its blink output as -4.

steps.title: See the recorded value on step 2
steps.caption: After disarming and stopping playback, hold step 2 at (2,4). Trig Params shows CC 1 at 64 with an L marker: the edited value was stored as a lock on that step.

assertion.characterisation: Current Trig Params screen marks the recorded step value with L.
Current Trig Params screen marks the recorded step value with L.
